independence_rule: Facts below were established from the local Book II chapter text before comparison with production JSON. Canonical IDs are normalization labels only and are never evidence sources.

functional_actors.source_display: Yoshioka messenger who reports Musashi's arrival

referenced_locations.source_display: Takase River / Sanjo area around Yomogi

facts.description: Seijuro, Toji, Ryohei and other Yoshioka students leave the school for the Kamo River pleasure district.
The Yoshioka party drinks, sings, boasts about swordsmanship and quarrels about the school's real standing.
Seijuro and Toji leave the first establishment and go to Yomogi while Ryohei remains with the other students.
Oko and Akemi receive Seijuro and Toji at Yomogi.
Seijuro pursues Akemi sexually while Toji and Oko encourage a match.
Matahachi quarrels with Oko over the teahouse, her relationship with Toji and his own dependence on her.
Matahachi remembers Otsu, his mother and Miyamoto, recognizes his decline and resolves to leave Oko.
Matahachi leaves by the kitchen door, returns for money, searches Oko's belongings and remains trapped by indecision.
A Yoshioka messenger reports at Yomogi that Miyamoto Musashi is at the school defeating its men and waiting for Seijuro.

functional_actors.source_display: Yoshioka servant who repeatedly questions Musashi at the gate

physical_locations.source_display: road between Kuyado and the burned Honnoji ruins

facts.description: Musashi enters the Yoshioka School, challenges Seijuro and defeats successive students with a wooden sword.
Several Yoshioka men are seriously wounded and two die after the bouts.
Seijuro and Toji return, learn the scale of the defeat and face anger over Seijuro's absence.
Senior members decide a direct Seijuro-Musashi fight is too risky and plan an ambush instead.
Yoshioka men surround Musashi's waiting room intending to kill him.
Musashi silently escapes by lifting floorboards and leaving before the ambush is sprung.
Pursuers stream through the gates and chase a fleeing figure through the back-street route toward Honnoji.
The pursuers seize Matahachi, mistaking him for Musashi, until Toji recognizes him from Yomogi.
Matahachi learns that Musashi is Takezo's new name and resolves to warn his old friend of the danger.
Denshichiro is reported away in Ise and is not physically present at the school.

functional_actors.source_display: palanquin bearers and porters supporting Osugi

physical_locations.source_display: western gate / Sannen and Chawan hill search area

facts.description: Musashi studies potters at work and takes their concentration and technique as a corrective to his own vanity.
A palanquin bearer asks Musashi's name and carries the information back toward Chawan Hill.
Musashi climbs through Kiyomizudera, prays for his sister and reflects on the life he wants to lead.
Porters surround Musashi near Hongando while crowds gather to watch.
Osugi and Gonroku arrive after their prolonged search and formally challenge Musashi over the Hon'iden grievance.
Musashi refuses to draw his sword against them and walks directly through the hostile crowd.
Musashi vanishes from the temple area while porters and supporters search the grounds until evening.
Jotaro visits the cheap inn, writes for the innkeeper and develops an immediate rapport with Musashi.
Jotaro states that his father is Aoki Tanzaemon, a former 2,500-koku samurai who lost his status; Musashi explicitly reflects on his own role in Tanzaemon's misfortune.
Jotaro asks to become Musashi's follower and Musashi conditionally agrees if the boy obtains his master's consent.
Musashi leaves the inn early for Nara, initially trying to avoid taking Jotaro with him.
Musashi passes the tightened Sanjo security checkpoint and reflects on his former Osaka allegiance.
Jotaro catches Musashi near Daigo, accuses him of breaking his promise and shows he received permission to leave; Musashi accepts him as follower.
Jotaro gives Musashi Matahachi's drunken letter warning him that the Yoshioka are hunting him.
At Rokuamida Musashi writes a provocative but formal reply to Seijuro and entrusts it to Jotaro.
Musashi also asks Jotaro to find Matahachi and invite him to a future meeting at the Gojo Avenue bridge.
Jotaro turns back toward Kyoto while Musashi continues toward Nara.
Jotaro finds Yomogi, asks Akemi for Matahachi and leaves Musashi's future meeting message with her.
From the written name and Jotaro's description, Akemi realizes Miyamoto Musashi is Takezo and revives her long-held hope of seeing him again.
Jotaro hitches a ride on a Kofukuji-bound oxcart, is thrown off and discovers he has lost the bamboo tube containing the Yoshioka reply.
Otsu tells Jotaro who found the tube; Shoda returns it unopened and rebukes the boy for neglecting his mission.
Jotaro travels with Otsu and Shoda and learns Otsu's name and that she supports herself by playing the flute.
At a teahouse the group hears a detailed warning about the dangerous ronin environment around Nara.
Shoda reveals his full identity and Yagyu service and invites Otsu to Koyagyu to play for Sekishusai.
Otsu accepts largely because the Yagyu household may have records or visitors who can lead her to Musashi.
They cross Uji Bridge and continue together toward the Kizu River.
At the Kizu River ferry Jotaro continues toward Nara while Otsu and Shoda take the Kasagi road toward Koyagyu.

functional_actors.source_display: young Ozoin monk who directs Musashi
Hozoin priests, visiting warriors and observers

physical_locations.source_display: private boardinghouse near the dumpling shop

facts.description: Musashi reaches Abura Hill, is directed through the Ozoin and learns the institutional relationship among In'ei, Nikkan and Inshun.
Musashi passes Nikkan working in the garden and reacts defensively to the force he senses from the old priest.
Musashi registers at the Hozoin, states his lack of a conventional teacher and accepts the risk of injury or death.
After Agon defeats other challengers, Musashi accepts a bout and kills him with a counterattack.
Nikkan explains that Musashi's excessive projected belligerence is itself a weakness and tells him he must learn to become weaker.
Nikkan identifies himself as Ozoin abbot, In'ei's old friend and the man who transmitted the Hozoin lance art to Inshun.
Although Musashi won physically against Agon, he leaves feeling spiritually outclassed by Nikkan.
Musashi returns to Hozoin to leave directions so Jotaro can find him near Sarusawa Pond.
Musashi moves to a private boardinghouse near Sarusawa Pond whose widowed owner values a male lodger as protection.
Three ronin flatter Musashi and propose a gambling-oriented public martial spectacle; he rejects them angrily.
Jotaro reaches Musashi, delivers the Yoshioka reply and reports that he could not find Matahachi.
The widow gives Musashi clothing and permits Jotaro to keep an old Noh mask before they prepare to leave.
The dumpling-maker's wife warns that Hozoin priests and ronin are waiting toward Hannya Plain because forged insults have been attributed to Musashi; he chooses to leave anyway.

functional_actors.source_display: five Nara officials serving Okubo Nagayasu

facts.description: Musashi sends the frightened Jotaro to watch from a hill rather than enter the expected ambush.
Dampachi approaches Musashi under a friendly pretext while attempting to guide him toward the waiting group.
Musashi detects the deception and kills Dampachi before entering the main gathering.
Musashi reaches the assembled priests and ronin; Inshun confronts him over the false reports and posters.
Musashi attacks the ronin first and kills roughly five or six before the survivors scatter.
Jotaro watches, prays for Musashi, realizes his teacher is winning and finally runs toward the battle when the Hozoin lancers move.
On Inshun's command the Hozoin lancers attack and finish the ronin rather than attacking Musashi.
Jotaro reaches Musashi and Inshun courteously introduces himself after the killing stops.
Nikkan arrives with Nara officials and reveals that he and Inshun deliberately used the false ambush as an opportunity to eliminate the troublesome ronin leadership with administrative cooperation.
Nikkan writes a sacred invocation on stones and has Jotaro scatter them among the dead before chanting for them.
Nikkan again warns Musashi that excessive strength and pride may kill him young and directs him toward Sekishusai and Lord Koizumi as models.
About ten days after Hannya Plain, Musashi and Jotaro stay in Koyagyu and survey the unusually stable, prosperous fief.
Musashi explains that serious martial study includes geography, agriculture, customs, governance and the condition of a lord's territory, not just fighting.
At the Wataya Jotaro meets Kocha and the children immediately quarrel.
In the communal bath Musashi overhears Denshichiro and companions belittle Sekishusai after Shoda politely refused their requested match.
Musashi recognizes the Yoshioka connection but remains unrecognized while vulnerable in the bath.
After comparing the Yagyu fief with Yoshioka arrogance, Musashi resolves that meeting Sekishusai will be his true test.
The chapter establishes Sekishusai's withdrawal from warfare, martial lineage under Lord Koizumi and philosophy of governing and self-control.
Otsu lives at Sekishusai's mountain house, plays flute for him and learns tea, poetry and flower arranging.
After Denshichiro persists in seeking a match, Sekishusai decides to send Otsu with a letter and a white peony instead of receiving him.
Otsu delivers Sekishusai's tactful refusal and peony to Denshichiro at the Wataya; he rejects the flower and gives up the visit angrily.
Otsu gives the rejected peony to Kocha rather than taking it back to the castle.
Musashi sees the peony, cuts the stem himself and recognizes that the original cut was made by a far superior swordsman.
The quality of the cut briefly undermines Musashi's confidence and convinces him the Yagyu are worthy opponents.
Returning from Wataya, Otsu meets Jotaro bathing in a river and invites him to visit the castle.
Sekishusai learns Denshichiro failed even to notice the peony's cut and judges that the Yoshioka house effectively ended with Kempo.
At the Yagyu dojo Kizaemon drives students through severe Shinkage-style training, illustrating the household's standard.
Jotaro enters the castle and forces Kizaemon to read Musashi's unusual letter asking who made the peony cut.
The Yagyu retainers compare the two cuts, learn Sekishusai made the original and infer that Musashi has unusual perception.
The retainers decide to invite Musashi informally to the Shin'indo for food, sake and martial conversation.
While waiting, Jotaro provokes and strikes the large black dog Taro; the dog attacks and injures him.

chapters.title: Jōtarō’s Revenge
historical_context: Sekigahara recollections during the Shin'indo discussion

physical_locations.source_display: castle grounds near dojo / Taro scene

facts.description: Jotaro returns to Wataya wounded and delivers Kizaemon's invitation without admitting how the dog injured him.
Kocha treats Jotaro's injuries; they admit liking each other and share an intimate childlike scene before Kocha's father interrupts them.
Musashi settles the Wataya bill and leaves with Jotaro at sunset for Koyagyu Castle.
Musashi presents Kizaemon's letter at the main gate and is admitted as an expected guest; Jotaro is left in an attendants' room.
The four senior retainers host Musashi with sake and question his ability to perceive the peony cut; the conversation becomes a mutual test.
Musashi says the perception cannot be explained without facing him with a sword, effectively issuing a challenge the hosts decline to take immediately.
Jotaro finds Taro and kills the dog as revenge for the earlier attack.
A dog keeper tries to kill Jotaro; Musashi intervenes, attacks another man and violently turns Jotaro himself into a projectile against the keeper.
The incident escalates until the four senior retainers disperse the crowd and place responsibility on themselves.
Musashi refuses detention and declares that his true purpose is to reach Sekishusai, treating the confrontation as one man against an entire castle.
Kimura attacks Musashi; Jotaro throws sand, Musashi evades, and all four retainers eventually encircle him.
A distant flute that Musashi recognizes as Otsu's breaks his concentration; Kimura tears his sleeve, after which Musashi escapes toward the inner-castle moat.

physical_locations.source_display: Koyagyu castle woods, valleys and back gate

facts.description: Musashi descends into the inner-castle moat, hides from torch-bearing searchers and later climbs out using branches as footholds.
Still determined to challenge Sekishusai, Musashi spends the night searching the outer castle grounds for the mountain house.
At dawn Musashi reaches Sekishusai's gate, reads the paired inscriptions and abandons the idea of barging in on the retired master.
Musashi sees Otsu and Jotaro emerge near the mountain house and hears them discussing the previous night's crisis without revealing himself.
Jotaro finds Musashi's towel, Otsu glimpses him, and Musashi flees despite their pursuit and repeated calls.
Otsu and Jotaro chase Musashi onto the Tsukigase-Iga back road until he disappears into wooded foothills.
At the roadside Otsu and Jotaro encounter Takuan, whose arrival follows an invitation from Sekishusai.
The chapter explains Takuan's long-standing connection with Munenori, Sekishusai and the Yagyu circle through Daitokuji/Sangen'in.
Otsu tells Takuan she remains determined to find Musashi; Takuan warns that her fixation may lead her toward self-destruction.
Otsu refuses to remain peacefully at Koyagyu; Jotaro chooses to continue with her after retrieving his mask, while Takuan accepts that he cannot stop them.
